featured_reviews.review_text:
The Carriage Repair Workshop at Lower Parel in Mumbai is a significant facility under Western Railway, dedicated to the maintenance and periodic overhauling (POH) of passenger coaches. Established in 1870 by the Bombay Baroda and Central India Railway, the workshop has a rich history of servicing and assembling various types of rolling stock, including locomotives, carriages, and wagons.

Over the years, the workshop has evolved to meet the changing needs of Indian Railways. It currently focuses on the POH of two main types of coaches: the older Integral Coach Factory (ICF) design and the modern Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) design, which are commonly used in premium trains like Rajdhani, Shatabdi, and Duronto Express. Annually, the facility overhauls approximately 1,700 coaches, including various classes such as General, Sleeper, and Air-Conditioned coaches. The workshop also manufactures wheel sets for its operations and supplies them to other divisions, with an average production of 12,000 wheel sets per year.

In recent years, the workshop has embraced modernization to enhance efficiency and maintenance quality. A proposal worth ₹176.81 crore has been submitted for approval, aiming to upgrade the facility's infrastructure. The modernization plan includes the construction of new sheds, the introduction of 'Coach Over Coach shunting' to reduce shunting time, and the installation of automated paint booths to improve paint quality and reduce cycle time. These upgrades are expected to increase the workshop's overhauling capacity by at least 20% and reduce the POH cycle time, ensuring safer and more reliable coach maintenance.

The workshop has also adopted innovative technologies for maintenance and safety. featured_reviews.name: Rashi Maheshwari
featured_reviews.review_text:
We've used GoMechanic twice for our car — once for a full service and once for a puncture repair. The first visit was fine and the team flagged a brake issue which we approved and paid ~₹20,000 to fix.

After the second visit (puncture repair), the car came back with a suspension issue that wasn't there before and was never flagged in any inspection. We're now being quoted ₹8,000 to fix it.

Both visits involved wheel removal and jacking — procedures that directly interface with suspension components. The timing and the fact that it was never flagged before makes it hard to believe this is unrelated to the workshop visit.

We've raised a formal complaint and are waiting for a response. Happy to update this review once the matter is resolved. Would appreciate a call from the GoMechanic team.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hello,
We sincerely apologize for the distress caused by the suspension issue following your puncture repair. We understand your concern regarding the timing and lack of prior flagging. Please contact our customer care team at customercare@gomechanic.in to help us investigate and resolve this promptly. We value your business.
Thank you
